tools/einstein/quiet-backoff/README.md: **Change after Moderator FAIL @6e9b0e49:** the default no longer backs off. Each 5-min tick does a conditional GET with `If-None-Match`. A 304 is free (it doesn't count against the GitHub rate limit) and means IDLE; a 200 with a new ETag means RUN the full gate check. Backoff is now opt-in (`QB_CAP>5`) and is not recommended, because every backoff setting regressed latency (table).
**Reproduce from this PR:** `python3 replay.py` (real data in `data/`):
Latency is mean push-detect latency, bootstrap 95% CI over pushes, 5 seeded runs (all 5 within ±0.01 of this one).
| Policy | Cron wakes/day | Full (rate-limited) checks/day | Mean latency [95% CI] | Max |
- Cron wakes (Actions minutes) are not reduced; only full checks and API quota are.
- Every wake-reducing setting gives a latency CI that doesn't overlap the baseline's.
- This is a simulation on real timestamps, and assumes 304s are free per GitHub's conditional-request docs.
- It is not wired into any workflow; that would touch locked paths.
- It is related to #295 (that PR caches PR-list ETags; this one gates the cron's full check on the head ref).
Tests: `python3 -m unittest test_quiet_backoff` (8 tests, including a replay-reproduction test).
tools/einstein/quiet-backoff/quiet_backo: Default (ETag mode): cron ticks every BASE min and does a conditional GET of the head ref with If-None-Match.
304 -> IDLE (free: 304s don't count against the GitHub rate limit); 200 with a new ETag/SHA -> RUN the full gate check.
Detect latency = the fixed-cron baseline; full checks only happen on change.
Optional backoff: QB_CAP>BASE doubles the tick interval while idle (fewer wakes, but higher latency; see README).
CLI: quiet_backoff.py due STATE            -> exit 0 if this tick should poll, 1 to skip (no API call)
quiet_backoff.py seen STATE STATUS ETAG -> prints RUN or IDLE and updates STATE"""
if cmd=="due": sys.exit(0 if due(st,now) else 1)
